summary: Confirmed DONE (fix in #710, 60633eff3, which is also in the Hub-vendored 7bc39eec3). The composer no longer runs discovery on mount. ChatComposer has no discovery hook, and ContextPickerButton enables it only on hover, focus or open. Client staleTime went from 30 s to 5 min, with revalidation on foreground, resume and online (Atom.swr focus respects staleTime). Background reads send {cached:true}, which the RPC routes to the cached discover. The server cache TTL went from 5 s to 2 min, is process-wide (built once in server.ts, and per-connection layers fork the runtime memo map) and is bypassed only by explicit refreshes. The finding's per-chat-entry probes (gh, glab, az auth) are gone. The only other mount-time reader at chat entry would be GitActionsControl, which the crown does not mount until the card opens or a branch flyout is hovered. The leftovers are small: PublishRepositoryDialog reads with the default enabled=true, the proposal's server background refresh was not done (and the 5-min client staleTime exceeds the 2-min server TTL, so a single client's revalidation almost always misses the server cache), the palette add-project view runs an uncached probe, and the discovery target ignores the thread's environmentId (true before the fix as well).

evidence.note: Discovery runs only when `open || wanted`; wanted is set by onPointerEnter/onFocus (lines 49-50). It shows the lists optimistically while discovery is pending. It is called with `undefined` target although props.environmentId is available.
Test asserts that mounting does not call manager.refresh and that clicking does.
5-min staleTime and 10-min idle TTL. The revalidate signal ticks on foreground/resume/online. The auto-refresh atom calls refresh(..., { cached: true }).
A disabled reader mounts a keepAlive idle atom and only observes shared state.
swr: revalidateOnFocus=true checks staleTime before refreshing, so focus events do not re-probe while data is fresh.
input.cached === true routes to sourceControlDiscovery.discover (Cache.get); anything else goes to refresh. No server test covers this routing.
TTL is 2 min. discover is Cache.get; refresh is invalidate+get. There is no stale-while-revalidate: the first cached read after expiry blocks on the full probe.

SourceControlDiscovery.layer is built once in the runtime graph. ws.ts:26-33 explains that per-connection layers fork the runtime memo map. Layer.effect is memoized by identity, so connections share one cache.
Forwards cached and dedupes in flight. An explicit refresh supersedes a cached one in flight. Covered by sourceControlDiscoveryState.test.ts:109-140.

PublishRepositoryDialog calls useSourceControlDiscovery() with enabled defaulting to true and is always rendered (open prop), so mounting GitActionsControl starts a cached discovery. GitActionsControl is mounted only through useOverviewPanelControls (ChatOverviewPanel.tsx:113-127), and the crown renders it only in the opened card (CrownOverview.tsx:75-76, CrownCard contentMounted) or in a hovered branch flyout.
The crown rail opens by default on wide desktop, but its card starts closed, so GitActionsControl, and with it discovery, is not mounted at chat entry.
The palette's 'Add project' source view calls refreshSourceControlDiscovery, the uncached full probe, each time it opens. It is user-initiated, infrequent and pre-existing.
Uncached refresh is called only after Bitbucket connect/disconnect and from the Rescan button. The settings page mount uses the cached auto-refresh.

fixDefects: None of these brings back the per-chat-entry cost. (1) apps/web/src/components/GitActionsControl.tsx:556: PublishRepositoryDialog reads discovery with enabled=true while closed. Opening the crown card, hovering the branch flyout or opening the phone overview sheet therefore starts a cached discovery even if Publish is never used. (2) The proposal's server background refresh was not implemented (SourceControlDiscovery.ts:146-160). Also, the 5-min client staleTime is longer than the 2-min server TTL, so a single client's revalidation (hover or foreground after 5 min) nearly always misses the server cache and runs the full gh/glab/az probe (~0.8-1.5 s). That happens off the paint path, at most once per 5 min. The `cached` path mainly helps multiple tabs or documents within 2 min. (3) CommandPaletteDialog.tsx:1265: the add-project source view always runs the uncached probe. (4) ContextPickerButton.tsx:25 and GitActionsControl.tsx:556 ignore the thread/dialog environmentId and target the primary node. This predates the fix (old ChatComposer.tsx:513 did the same), but for a remote-environment thread the remote gating reflects the wrong node. (5) No server test covers the providerRpc cached-vs-refresh routing.
implementationSketch: All optional and low priority. (a) GitActionsControl.tsx:556: change to `useSourceControlDiscovery({ environmentId: props.environmentId }, { enabled: props.open })`. Nothing outside the dialog reads it, so the publish menu gating is unaffected. Extend an existing GitActionsControl browser test: with the dialog closed, spy on sourceControlDiscoveryManager.refresh and assert it is not called. (b) ContextPickerButton.tsx:25: pass `{ environmentId: props.environmentId }` so remote-environment threads gate on their own node. (c) Server SWR in apps/server/src/sourceControl/SourceControlDiscovery.ts: keep `{ result, at }` in a Ref. `discover` returns the stored result immediately when present; when it is older than the TTL, it forks one background refresh in the layer scope, deduped with a Semaphore(1) or an in-flight Deferred. `refresh` stays invalidate+probe and updates the Ref. As a simpler alternative, raise SOURCE_CONTROL_DISCOVERY_CACHE_TTL to at least the client staleTime (e.g. 6 min). Test with TestClock in SourceControlDiscovery.test.ts: a stale cached read returns the old value without waiting and triggers exactly one probe. Add a providerRpc/ws test showing cached:true does not re-probe while an omitted flag does. (d) CommandPaletteDialog.tsx:1265: optionally call sourceControlDiscoveryManager.refresh(target, undefined, { cached: true }) and keep the explicit rescan in Settings.
decisionReason: Pure client/server caching and targeting tweaks. No auth/E2EE, Hub protocol or hosted lifecycle impact. The RPC field is additive, and old servers ignore it because excess struct keys are ignored.
